what_it_does: Regular expressions (patterns used to search text, like finding all email addresses in a document) can be compiled into compact bit-level programs that process many characters at once — a technique called bitparallel matching. GPUs (graphics chips repurposed for general computation) are good at running many such operations in parallel, but the naive approach loads each chunk of text from memory multiple times — once per pattern instruction — wasting bandwidth. This paper introduces an interleaved execution model where one chunk of text is loaded once and all pattern instructions are applied to it before moving on, dramatically improving data reuse. Three supporting techniques handle the tricky dependencies that arise between text chunks, reorganize the instruction order to reduce synchronization, and skip chunks that are guaranteed to produce all-zero (empty) results — cutting unnecessary work.
